contexts.text: From a Community Request to a Lean Tactic: -Assisted Norm Arithmetic
A community request for norm automation
A finite core with checked certificates

A 2020 Lean community discussion asked for automation that finds hidden decompositions in norm inequalities. We used artificial intelligence (AI) coding agents to develop , a reusable Lean tactic for the normed-space part of this request. AI assisted development. The resulting tactic runs without a language model and constructs proofs that Lean checks. We give the implementation, its finite real-space core, and an evaluation against existing mathlib proofs.

A verified local patch replaces proof spans in files and removes code lines after preparation and imports. Across 40 paired passes with built dependencies, the ratio of mean original and replacement compilation times is . The conditional paired 95% interval is FORMULA . This case study measures the resulting artifact, without a controlled comparison of AI and human development effort.

In May 2020, Heather Macbeth asked for a Lean tactic that could find decompositions for norm inequalities . The example was FORMULA . Its useful identity is FORMULA . The discussion identified this decomposition search as a missing step in automation. The later discussion also proposed normed-algebra reasoning with products, which remains outside our core. We address the decomposition-search part of the request.

We used AI coding agents to build a reusable tactic for this kind of proof. The resulting finds rational coefficients and constructs a proof from them. This checked source example proves the requested inequality. Here FORMULA is a real seminormed space.

The contribution is a case study in AI-assisted development of proof infrastructure for an existing community request. We give a checked certificate interface, a finite characterization of the core fragment, and a reproducible library evaluation. The tactic runs as ordinary Lean code, without a model call at proof time. Each successful invocation produces a proof term checked by Lean's kernel .

ChatGPT generated the starter, and Codex with GPT-6 assisted subsequent implementation and evaluation. The repository records these tools in its development guide and commit history. The first interface used explicit upper bounds. The project then added automatic bound selection, a shared certificate layer, and bounded extensions. AI agents also helped develop and review source replacements for the library evaluation.

One recorded regression concerned definitionally equal vector terms written through function aliases. Certificate construction failed on these terms. The correction checked identities during elaboration and used matching normalization settings. Regression tests then passed a complete build with warnings treated as errors. Negative tests also checked that explicit fact lists excluded omitted norm bounds. Appendix links the design decisions and failure-to-repair records.

The library experiment checks a combined source patch and measures its compilation cost. These checks support correctness and utility of the artifact. They do not measure AI's effect on development time.

In Lean, IDENTIFIER checks vector identities, and IDENTIFIER combines scalar inequalities. The IDENTIFIER tactic provides structural inequality automation. Our tactic searches for decomposition constraints before these proof checks. Its contribution is an AI-assisted implementation, a checked certificate design, and an evaluation against library proofs.

The artifact addresses a documented normed-space request. The patch is local, with no mathlib acceptance claim. We did not run a separate comparison against other Lean tactics.
